title: Travel Planning
searchIntent: grok bot to plan a trip
intro: Trip planning splits into two jobs that look similar and are not. Research — where to go, what is worth doing, building an itinerary that survives contact with real opening hours — is genuinely helped by an agent that can browse and hold the whole trip in context. Monitoring is the other one: watching a route for a price you named, tracking a booked flight for changes, noticing when a points redemption becomes available. The second is where a bot beats a person, because it is patient in a way you are not. Most listings here do research; fewer do monitoring well, and monitoring is the one you would actually keep past a single trip. As with any bot given a booking site, read carefully before granting anything that can confirm a reservation on your behalf.

bots.fitReason: Pulls live flights, hotels, ground transport and official event tickets, compares real prices and prefers local official sites — the closest thing here to a full trip desk. Research and booking legwork only; it does not sit and watch a route for the price you named.

Award-travel and logistics specialist that reasons in AAdvantage, Amex and cabin availability rather than generic web results. Caveat: it is hard-wired to a DCA/IAD/BWI home airport and one loyalty stack, so anyone outside that has to rewrite its assumptions.

Arranges flights, rail and hotels with both the cheap route and the easy route side by side, checking cash fares against the miles and campaigns you actually hold. Japanese-language and Japan-centric, which is either the point or a dealbreaker.

Configured per trip with your park days, Early Entry and must-do rides, then plans around wait times — real itinerary work, just for exactly one destination. Useless for anything outside Walt Disney World.

Handles the redemption side: keeping card and airline points optimised so award value is not left on the table. It is a points brain, not an itinerary builder, and there is no claim it watches for award space opening up.

Keeps a Notion travel log, scores cities and does light itinerary prep, so it answers 'where have I been and what fits me' well. Honest caveat: it is closer to a trip archive than a planner, and does no price or booking monitoring.
